name_reason: Compliant fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> name; accurately describes a leaf accessor that returns an entry of the job-allowed-items table indexed by job_id. No Ghidra address residue in the name (the '7' stride is not in the name; descriptor terms are all semantic).
purpose: Leaf .object3 data-table accessor: returns a pointer to the 7-byte job_allowed_items_table entry for a given job_id.
logic_summary: Computes base 0x6188A + job_id*7 and returns it as a byte pointer (no loads, no side effects). The 7-byte stride entry holds 6 allowed item-category bytes (caller scans them; 0xFF = empty slot) followed by a 1-byte stride separator at byte[6]. job_id range 0..0x1A (27 jobs). Verified table base 0x6188A = 0x615FD + 0x28D; data at 0x6188A confirms 7-byte-stride entries (e.g. job 0 dragon = ff ff ff ff ff ff, job 1 swordsman = 01 15 16 ff ff ff).

params.name: job_id
params.semantics: Job/class ID, range 0..0x1A (27 jobs per assets/jobs.md). Caller passes data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr[char_idx].bJob_id. Used as the table index (job_id*7).
params.reason: Descriptive, matches actual usage as a job index; no address residue.

returns.semantics: Pointer to the job's 7-byte entry in job_allowed_items_table (base 0x6188A). Caller reads the first 6 bytes as allowed item-category bytes (0xFF = empty slot); byte[6] is the stride separator.

comment_original_issue: Original src comment was correct but terse ('Returns pointer to 7-byte allowed-items list for job_id'); it omitted the job_id range, the 6-allowed-bytes + 1-separator layout, the 0xFF empty-slot sentinel, and the caller (fd2_check_job_can_equip_item).
notes: Bytecode-identical to fd2_get_spell_effect_entry @ 0x4E516 (same bb_hash); distinguished only by table base. Ghidra decompile anchors the base symbol to data_orphan_615fd_... + 0x28D, but src already uses the proper symbol data_fd2_battle_job_allowed_items_table -- no rename needed. Plate is already detailed and consistent with the refined src comment, so left untouched.
